CommandEntry.description: One command or skill and whether ADE can hand it to the provider.

argument_hint.description: The provider's argument hint, such as `<file>`.

reason.description: Why the entry cannot be invoked, or a caveat when it can.

`command.invoke`: hand a listed command or skill to the Conversation's
provider in its native form. The invocation joins the Conversation's
prompt queue under the derived queue ID `<operation_id>:command`.

arguments.description: Free text passed after the command, as the provider's own input would.

name.description: The entry name as `command.list` reported it, without a leading slash.

native_text.description: The exact text queued for the provider.

CommandKind.description: Whether an entry is a slash command or a skill.

entries.description: Sorted by kind, then name, then path.

skipped.description: Provider paths or scopes this listing did not read, and why.

CommandListRequest.description:
`command.list`: the commands and skills available to one Conversation.
Reads provider paths and the skill catalog; writes nothing.

CommandNativeCatalog.description:
What the provider itself reports about its commands. ADE does not yet ask
a live provider session for its list, so built-in and plugin commands are
not shown and cannot be invoked through ADE.

method.description: The provider method that would list them, when one exists.

catalog_name.description: The ADE catalog bundle with the same content, if any.

content_hash.description: The skill bundle content hash, when the entry is a valid skill.

path.description: The file or directory ADE read.

oneOf.description: A command file in a directory the provider reads.
A skill directory in a root the provider reads.
A bundle in ADE's skill catalog that is not in any path the provider reads.

commits.description: Commits reachable from HEAD and not from the base.

truncated.description: More files changed than the reply carries (2 000).

oneOf.description: ADE cannot prove what was committed, for example without a base commit.

CommittedFile.description: A file a run committed since the group started.

code.description: The `git diff --name-status` letter, such as A, M, D or T.

Config.description:
A repository's stored lifecycle configuration. Fields added after the
first release are omitted from the wire while they hold their defaults.

branch_prefix.description: Prefix for branches that `worktree.create` names, such as `ade/`.

default_base.description:
Start point for `worktree.create` when the request names none; `HEAD`
when absent.

directory.description: Parent directory for new trees; the repository's parent when absent.

resources.description:
Ignored local resources, such as `.env` files or `node_modules`, and
how each reaches a tree ADE creates. Nothing ignored is copied or
linked unless a rule names it.

setup.description:
Hooks run in order inside a new tree after Git creates it. The tree is
ready for an Agent only after every hook exits 0.

teardown.description:
Hooks run in order inside a tree before ADE removes it. A failed hook
keeps the tree.

import.description: Importing native history that ADE did not create.

The caller's operation ID. The daemon keeps a receipt under it: a

A saved preset whose provider, model and permission mode the

ConversationDeleteRequest.description:
`conversation.delete`: delete a Conversation that is not running a turn.
An idle Agent is stopped first. The daemon removes its messages, pending
requests, drafts, draft history and stashes, queue, send intents and
snooze, detaches its windows, and leaves a tombstone: every later read,
write, page or search that names the Conversation is refused as deleted.
Attachment payloads stay until retention reclaims them.

operation_id.description:
The caller's operation ID. The deletion and its receipt commit in one
transaction; a retry with the same ID returns the recorded reply.

attachments_left_for_retention.description:
Live attachment payloads the deletion left in place. Nothing references
them any more, so retention reclaims each once its grace period passes.

deleted_at.description: When the tombstone was written, in Unix milliseconds.

ConversationDeletedFrame.description:
The `conversation_deleted` feed frame. A client drops its view of the
Conversation; a snapshot or page read earlier is stale.

windows_detached.description: Windows that showed the Conversation and now show none.

before.description: Return messages with a sequence below this one.

history_epoch.description:

older page (`before` set) is refused once a rewind replaced history,
so a client never splices pages of two histories together.

limit.description: Page size; the daemon uses 50 when it is absent.

before_message_id.description: The first removed message: the user message that started `turn_id`.

native_session.description:

state_token.description: Names the previewed history; a rewind refuses a history that changed.

turn_id.description: The provider turn the rewind returns to before.

files.description: The checkpoint restore preview; present for an available file rewind.

than a managed account.

The calendar day the turn was first observed, shifted by
`utc_offset_minutes`, as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

UsageLimitWindow.description: One rate-limit window as the provider last reported it.

account_id.description: Null for the provider's own login.

limit_id.description: The provider's name for the window, such as `five_hour` or `codex:primary`.

observed_at.description:
When the daemon received this report. Limits are only as fresh as the
provider's last report; no probe runs between turns.

reset_since_observed.description: True when `resets_at` has passed, so `used_percent` is out of date.

status.description: The provider's own status word, such as `allowed_warning` or `rejected`.

used_percent.description: 0 to 100. Null when the latest report did not include it.

UsageLimitsRequest.description: `usage.limits`: the latest rate-limit windows each provider reported.

UsageMeasure.description: A token total over a group of turns.

unreported_turns.description:
Turns in the group that did not report this figure. The value is
complete only when this is 0.

value.description: The sum over turns that reported this figure; null when none did.

UsageRecording.description: Whether the daemon could record every report it received since it started.

dropped_batches.description:
Event batches whose usage could not be saved since the daemon started.
Their turns are missing from every figure.

UsageScope.description: Which agents a turn's figures cover.

oneOf.description: Only the conversation's own agent; subagent and helper calls are excluded.
The agent and every subagent or internal call the provider counted.

UsageSummaryRequest.description: `usage.summary`: aggregate recorded turns by one dimension.

utc_offset_minutes.description: Shifts day boundaries for `group_by: day`, from -840 to 840; 0 when absent.

UsageTokens.description:
Token counts for one turn. `input` counts every prompt token, including
tokens read from or written to the prompt cache; `cached_input` and
`cache_write` are parts of it. `reasoning` is part of `output`. A null
field was not reported by the provider.

UsageTurn.description: One turn's recorded usage and its provenance.

account_id.description: The managed account the turn ran on; null for the provider's own login.

note.description: Why a figure is partial or unavailable, when the daemon knows.

observed_at.description: When the daemon first observed the turn, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

reported.description: False when the provider reported nothing for this turn.

source.description: The native event the figures came from, such as `thread/tokenUsage/updated`.

next_cursor.description: Null when no more records remain.

UsageTurnsRequest.description: `usage.turns`: one page of per-turn records, most recently observed first.

cursor.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page for the same filters.

limit.description: Page size, 1 to 100; the daemon uses 50 when it is absent.

WaitState.description: What a wait observed. Only `pending` means the caller should ask again.

oneOf.description:
The child asked a question or needs approval. Answer each request once
with `agent.answer` on the child Conversation.
The message will not progress without intervention.
The deadline passed while the turn was still pending.
The child Conversation no longer exists.

WindowCloseRequest.description: `window.close`: forget a window's record, unless it is the last one.

window.description: The window record, in the shape `catalog.get` lists it.

WorkspaceChoice.description:
Where the child works, stated explicitly. Parallel children in the same
workspace share its files; ADE never merges their edits.

oneOf.description: The parent's workspace.

A new linked worktree made by a succeeded `worktree.switch` with
`create`, then opened as `workspace_id`. The daemon verifies both.

WorkspaceMode.description: How the child's workspace was chosen.

WorkspaceOpenRequest.description: `workspace.open`: register a folder, or return the workspace already at it.

path.description: The folder to open; the daemon canonicalizes it.

WorkspaceRebindEntry.description: One restored workspace. `rebindable` says a saved physical identity exists.

WorkspaceRebindListRequest.description: `workspace.rebind.list`: restored workspaces and whether each needs a path.

WorkspaceRebindRequest.description: `workspace.rebind`: bind a restored workspace to a verified directory.

WorktreeAdoptRequest.description: `worktree.adopt`: take ADE removal authority over an existing linked tree.

confirm_path.description:
Must equal the canonical form of `path`. Optional in Rust only so a
missing value keeps the daemon's own error message.

operation_id.description:
The caller's operation ID. The daemon keeps a receipt under it: a
retry with the same ID and payload returns the recorded outcome, and
the same ID with another payload is a conflict.

WorktreeArchive.description: The `worktree.archived` reply, newest first, at most 200 records.

WorktreeArchiveEntry.description:
The record ADE keeps for a tree it removed. The branch, unless deleted,
is the way back to the work.

head.description: The commit the tree had checked out when it was removed.

operation_id.description: The `worktree.remove` or `worktree.cleanup` operation that removed it.

WorktreeArchivedRequest.description: `worktree.archived`: list the archive records of removed trees.

WorktreeCarryEntry.description: One changed path in the source.

staged.description: The index differs from `HEAD`. Carried changes arrive staged.

unstaged.description: The working tree differs from the index.

WorktreeCarryPreview.description:
The `worktree.carry.preview` reply. Ignored files are never listed or
carried; ignored-resource rules handle them.

head.description: The source commit; pass it as `expect_head`. `null` when unborn.

WorktreeCarryPreviewRequest.description:
`worktree.carry.preview`: list a tree's uncommitted changes and whether
each can be carried. Changes nothing.

paths.description:
Paths relative to the tree root to select; every change when absent.
A directory selects the changes beneath it.

source.description: The tree whose changes would move: the primary checkout or a linked tree.

WorktreeCarryRequest.description:
`worktree.carry`: move uncommitted changes from `source` into the clean,
ADE-owned tree `target`. The changes are first saved as a commit under
`refs/ade/carry/…`, which ADE never deletes, then applied to the target
and verified. The source is cleaned only when `clean_source` is true, the
target verified exactly, and the source is unchanged since the snapshot.
A failure never discards anything.

clean_source.description: Remove the carried changes from the source after verification.

expect_head.description: The source `HEAD` the caller previewed; a different `HEAD` refuses.

operation_id.description: Caller-owned operation ID; `request_id` is accepted as an alias.

paths.description: As in `worktree.carry.preview`; every change when absent.

WorktreeCleanupPlan.description: The `worktree.cleanup.plan` reply: every linked tree, primary excluded.

WorktreeCleanupPlanRequest.description:
`worktree.cleanup.plan`: classify every linked tree for cleanup without
changing anything.

delete_branch.description: Branch policy for every removed tree; `keep` when absent.

operation_id.description: Caller-owned operation ID; `request_id` is accepted as an alias.

paths.description: One to 32 tree paths, each from `worktree.cleanup.plan`.

WorktreeConfigInput.description:
The configuration a caller sends. Absent fields take their defaults; the
stored form is [`Config`].

branch_prefix.description:
Prefix for branches `worktree.create` names: letters, digits, `.`,
`_`, `-` and `/`, at most 64 bytes.

default_base.description: Start point for `worktree.create` when the request names none.

directory.description: Parent directory for new trees; the repository's parent when absent.

resources.description:
Ignored-resource rules, at most 64, applied in each tree ADE creates
before its setup hooks.

setup.description: Setup hooks, at most 8, run in order inside each tree ADE creates.

teardown.description: Teardown hooks, at most 8, run in order before ADE removes a tree.

timeout_seconds.description: Git command timeout; the daemon accepts 5 to 300.

WorktreeCreateRequest.description:
`worktree.create`: create a branch and a linked tree from the repository's
naming defaults, then run its setup hooks. With neither `name` nor
`branch`, the daemon generates the first free `wt-N` name.

base.description: Start point; the configured `default_base`, then `HEAD`, when absent.

branch.description: An exact branch name, used without the prefix. Conflicts with `name`.

fetch.description:
Start from a ref fetched from a configured remote, such as a pull
request head. Conflicts with `base`. Only the fetch is performed; ADE
adds no pull-request workflow.

name.description: A workspace name; the branch is the configured prefix plus its slug.

operation_id.description: Caller-owned operation ID; `request_id` is accepted as an alias.

path.description: Absolute path for the tree, directly inside the configured directory.

WorktreeFetchSource.description:
A ref to fetch from a configured remote into `refs/ade/fetched/…`. The
new branch starts at the fetched commit.

ref.description:
A full ref on the remote, such as `refs/pull/12/head` or
`refs/merge-requests/12/head`.

remote.description: A remote name from `git remote`; URLs are refused.

WorktreeGetRequest.description: `worktree.get`: read a registered repository's lifecycle state.

WorktreeHookProgress.description:
A hook that is still running: which one, how far the operation has got,
and the latest output, bounded to its last 16 KiB.

completed.description: The hooks of this phase that have finished, without their output.

index.description: The hook's position in its phase, from 0.

output.description: The last 16 KiB of stdout and stderr, interleaved as they arrived.

path.description: The tree the hook runs in.

total.description: How many hooks the phase has configured.

WorktreeHookRun.description:
One hook run, as recorded in an operation's `result.hooks` or in a
cleanup tree's `hooks`.

output.description: The last 64 KiB of stdout, then of stderr. `worktree_state` omits it.

WorktreeItem.description: One entry of `git worktree list`, with ADE's ownership and setup state.

ade_owned.description: Whether ADE holds removal authority over this tree.

phase.description: The tree's lifecycle phase, for trees ADE created or ran hooks in.

WorktreeOperation.description: One lifecycle operation from the ledger. The daemon stores this shape.

request.description: The request as the caller sent it, including `op`.

result.description:
Command output and its `value`; `null` until the command runs.
`worktree_state` omits `stdout` and `stderr`.

running_hook.description:
The setup or teardown hook the operation is running now. Present only
while a hook runs; the daemon keeps it in memory, so a restarted daemon
reports the interrupted operation without it.

WorktreeOperationRequest.description: `worktree.operation`: read one lifecycle operation receipt in full.

operation_id.description: The operation's ID; `request_id` is accepted as an alias.

WorktreeOperationStatus.description: A lifecycle operation's status in its ledger.

oneOf.description:
The tree was removed but its branch was kept, or a cleanup archived
some of its trees and not others.
The daemon stopped while the operation ran; inspect before retrying.

WorktreePhase.description:
Where a tree stands in ADE's setup and teardown lifecycle. Only `ready`
admits an Agent.

oneOf.description: Names are recorded and Git is creating the tree.
Setup hooks are running.
A setup hook failed or timed out. The tree is kept; retry `worktree.setup`.
Setup stopped with an unknown outcome. Inspect the tree before retrying.
Teardown hooks or the removal are running.
A teardown hook failed or timed out. The tree is kept.
Teardown or removal stopped with an unknown outcome.

WorktreeRebindCandidate.description: One lifecycle repository in the rebind catalog.

rebindable.description: Whether the saved source identity survives, so a rebind can be verified.

WorktreeRebindListRequest.description: `worktree.rebind.list`: list lifecycle repositories and whether each needs a rebind.

WorktreeRebindRequest.description: `worktree.rebind`: bind a restored lifecycle repository to a verified checkout.

WorktreeRefreshRequest.description: `worktree.refresh`: re-read the Git worktree listing under the repository lock.

operation_id.description: Caller-owned operation ID; `request_id` is accepted as an alias.

WorktreeRemoveRequest.description: `worktree.remove`: remove a clean ADE-owned linked tree.

delete_branch.description:
Branch policy; the daemon uses `keep` when it is absent. The daemon
reads the raw string so an unknown policy keeps its own error message.

force.description: Forced removal is unavailable; `true` is rejected.

operation_id.description: Caller-owned operation ID; `request_id` is accepted as an alias.

WorktreeRepository.description: A registered lifecycle repository. Device and inode identities are decimal strings.

root.description: The primary checkout, where lifecycle commands run.

source_common_dir.description: The common directory before the first rebind.

WorktreeRepositoryRequest.description:
`worktree.repository`: register the Git repository containing `path`, or
return the one already registered for its common directory.

WorktreeResourcesApplyRequest.description:
`worktree.resources.apply`: apply the repository's ignored-resource rules
to an ADE-owned tree, such as an adopted one. Existing files are never
replaced.

operation_id.description: Caller-owned operation ID; `request_id` is accepted as an alias.

WorktreeSetupRequest.description:
`worktree.setup`: run the setup hooks again in an ADE-owned tree, such as
one whose setup failed or was interrupted. Only a full success makes it ready.

operation_id.description: Caller-owned operation ID; `request_id` is accepted as an alias.

WorktreeState.description:
A repository's lifecycle state: the reply to every command except
`worktree.operation` and `worktree.rebind.list`.

busy.description: Whether a lifecycle or review operation holds the repository.

operations.description: The newest 100 operations, newest first, without command output.

worktrees.description: The cached Git listing, primary checkout first.

WorktreeSwitchRequest.description:
`worktree.switch`: check out `target` in a linked tree, creating the branch
when `create` is true.

base.description: Start point for a new branch; the daemon uses `HEAD` when it is absent.

operation_id.description: Caller-owned operation ID; `request_id` is accepted as an alias.

path.description: Absolute path for a new tree, directly inside the configured directory.

target.description: A branch name, or the path of an existing linked tree.

XtermReplayRecovery.description: Recorded output and resizes from the start of the process, up to a limit.

complete.description: False when the output passed `limit_bytes`; `events` is then empty.

through_offset.description: The live-output offset the replay reaches.
